In Chapter 6, we calculated the work done by a constant force of magnitude F in moving an object through a distance d as W = Fd. That formula holds only if the force is directed along the line of motion. If a force F moving an object through a displacement D = r PQ has some other direction, the work is performed by the component of F in the direction of D.
